headline: Inflation breaks six percent, Nvidia's chief quits, oil back near 95 dollars

segments.title: The big picture
segments.script:
Good morning. It's Friday, the thirteenth of November, and here is your Market Brief.

Three things matter most today. First, retail inflation has broken through the Reserve Bank's upper limit of 6 percent for the first time in about two years. It rose to 6.09 percent in October, from 5.54 percent in September, and economists now openly talk about another rate hike in December.

Second, a shock from America. Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang, has resigned, and finance chief Colette Kress has stepped in as interim head. The stock fell as much as 14 percent before recovering to end about 4 percent lower.

And third, oil is climbing again. Brent crude is back near 95 dollars a barrel after fresh Houthi attacks on Saudi energy facilities, which is weighing on Indian shares this morning.

segments.title: How markets closed
segments.script:
Thursday was the third straight day of gains. The Nifty closed near 25,300 and the Sensex near 81,900. Real estate led the way, with the realty index jumping 4 percent as Oberoi, Sobha and Lodha rose about 5 percent each. So far this November, realty stocks are up 14 percent, against a 9.6 percent rise in the Nifty. Insurers also rallied up to 5 percent after life insurers' new business premiums grew about 26 percent in October. Paytm jumped over 7 percent to close at 1,925 rupees, its highest close since it listed in 2021.

This morning the mood has turned. The Sensex fell around 400 points early, with the Nifty slipping near 25,150, as the inflation number and costlier oil hit bank, auto and realty stocks, each down about 1 percent. Oil-sensitive names like Bharat Petroleum and IndiGo fell more than 2 percent. Power stocks went the other way, up 1 percent, after reports that a first-of-its-kind 1,150 kilovolt transmission project worth 68,816 crore rupees was approved. Steady buying by foreign institutional investors and a dip in crude then helped the Sensex climb back about 500 points from the day's low, with the Nifty back above 25,200.

The rupee slipped past 94 to the dollar on Thursday, closing at 94.04, as American bond yields rose. As for levels, Moneycontrol's trading plan sees resistance for the Nifty at 25,400 to 25,500, and support at 25,100 to 25,000.

segments.title: IPOs and deals
segments.script:
One new issue for your calendar. Crystal Crop Protection has fixed a price band of 259 to 272 rupees a share for its 456 crore rupee public issue. It opens on Wednesday, the eighteenth, and closes on the twentieth, with the anchor book on Monday, the seventeenth.

Overseas, the biggest share sale of the year is drawing heavy demand. Anthropic's public offering is reported to be about six times oversubscribed, according to Bloomberg. Livemint reports it could value the company at up to 1.4 trillion dollars, with a proposed price of 74 dollars and a Nasdaq listing.

Back home, Meesho shares rose 1 percent after a block deal of about 1,885 crore rupees, covering 1.65 percent of the company. And LIC, Meesho and Coforge are in focus ahead of the November index rejig by MSCI.

segments.title: Results roundup
segments.script:
Now to the September quarter results, starting with telecom and electric vehicles, where the news was disappointing. Vodafone Idea posted a wider-than-expected loss, and the shares fell about 3.5 percent. Nomura kept its neutral rating, pointing to margin pressure and weak growth in average revenue per user. Ola Electric's revenue fell 39 percent, though its loss narrowed to 362 crore rupees from 418 crore a year ago. The stock slid nearly 7 percent.

Capital goods had a much better day. Hitachi Energy India's profit rose 21 percent and revenue jumped about 64 percent. New orders grew 86 percent to about 4,121 crore rupees, taking its order book to a record of about 33,335 crore. The shares rose as much as 9 percent. Automotive Axles climbed nearly 15 percent after profit rose two-thirds to 60 crore rupees on revenue up 43.5 percent.

Among state-run companies, MSTC hit its 20 percent upper limit after profit rose about 58 percent to 74.92 crore rupees. Rail Vikas Nigam was mixed, with profit up 10 percent to about 254 crore, even as revenue fell 8 percent.

In consumer names, Page Industries hit its 10 percent lower limit on Thursday after profit grew just 4 percent to 202.5 crore rupees, though it declared a dividend of 150 rupees a share. HSBC and Nomura still keep buy ratings on it.

segments.title: Economy and policy
segments.script:
Let's go back to inflation, because it shapes everything else this morning. Food inflation climbed to 8.94 percent in October, from 7.74 percent in September. Onion prices are up 116 percent, and six states now have inflation above 7 percent. This is the ninth straight monthly rise. Economists quoted by the Economic Times expect retail inflation to average about 6.2 percent in the October to December quarter.

So what will the Reserve Bank do? It already raised the repo rate by a quarter of a percentage point in October. ICICI Bank now expects another quarter-point hike in December. State Bank of India's economists have halved their own forecast, from half a point to a quarter point, because pressure on the rupee has eased and foreign money is flowing back. Nuvama warns that uneven monsoons and a possible El Niño add upside risk to food prices.

On growth, the news is better. SBI Research expects the economy grew 7.8 percent in the September quarter, above the Reserve Bank's estimate of 7.2 percent. And the International Monetary Fund has raised its estimate of India's potential growth to 6.8 percent.

On tax, the government's direct tax target for this year is 26.97 lakh crore rupees, and only about 53 percent had come in by the tenth of November. Experts say the second half, especially advance tax, will be make-or-break.

A few policy items. The Reserve Bank is working on rules to stop private equity firms from controlling several non-bank lenders at once, according to a report. The Cabinet approved a rabi fertiliser subsidy of 62,370 crore rupees, up 64 percent, keeping a bag of di-ammonium phosphate at 1,350 rupees, plus a 5,000 crore rupee guarantee fund for MUDRA loans. And a NITI Aayog report says the production-linked incentive schemes have created about 8.49 lakh jobs, just 28 percent of the target, though about 70 percent of segments are on track. The government is now looking at tweaks to the programme.

segments.title: Around the world
segments.script:
Now to the world, and Nvidia. Jensen Huang's resignation sent the chipmaker down as much as 14 percent, but dip buyers stepped in and it closed about 4 percent lower, still above a 4 trillion dollar market value. Rivals gained, with AMD up nearly 6 percent and Broadcom up about 5.5 percent. US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is due to testify before Congress on the matter. Wall Street ended modestly lower, while Asian tech stocks bounced back this morning.

On oil, Brent is around 95 dollars after the Houthi attacks and shipping disruption near the Strait of Hormuz. Even so, it is on track for a second weekly fall, as President Trump says he will keep the blockade on Iran and that no deal is needed. Remember, Brent touched 118 dollars on the thirtieth of October. One more oil note: India's crude imports from the Gulf, at 2.1 million barrels a day this month, have overtaken Russian supplies for the first time since the Iran war.

The American 10-year bond yield has jumped to about 5.1 percent as traders price in further Federal Reserve hikes. And gold has slipped below 3,900 dollars an ounce, its lowest in over a year.

segments.title: Stories you're following
segments.script: An update on the India–US trade deal you're following. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said on Thursday that India will have one of the best trade deals with the US in every respect, though changes in American tariffs have meant more negotiation since February's framework. And former American diplomat Nisha Biswal says both sides want to conclude the first phase by the G20 Summit in Florida, while warning that significant issues remain.

segments.title: Your money
segments.script:
Finally, your money. After October's rate hike, major banks have raised fixed deposit rates on select tenures, and lending rates have begun to inch up too. Some small finance banks now offer up to 8.25 percent.

If you hold the 2018-19 Series Three sovereign gold bond, today is its final redemption. Livemint says investors stand to earn capital gains of up to 348 percent, before counting interest.

A worrying sign from mutual funds. New systematic investment plans opened in October fell to an 18-month low, while closures were the highest since April 2025. Active accounts dropped from about 10.89 crore to 10.8 crore. On the other side, arbitrage funds pulled in 3,929 crore rupees, reversing September's outflows. And if your fund holds Nvidia, note that 13 Indian schemes and exchange traded funds own the stock, some with up to 12 percent exposure.

On tax, if you plan to buy Anthropic shares from India, Livemint reminds you of 20 percent tax collected at source on remittances above 10 lakh rupees under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, Indian capital gains tax, American withholding on dividends, and foreign asset disclosure in your return. Industry bodies are lobbying ahead of next year's Budget, with the PHD Chamber seeking to scrap long-term capital gains tax on equities and cut the short-term rate to 10 percent.

That's the brief. Today, watch whether the Nifty holds the 25,000 to 25,100 zone as oil and inflation fears test the rally, and how Nvidia trades after Lutnick's testimony. Next week, the Crystal Crop anchor book on Monday, and every word from the Reserve Bank ahead of December. Have a good Friday.
